nodes.label: Applied Architecture Authority

nodes.label: Local Authority Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Operational evidence outranks explanatory material, and this folder must not become a second source of truth.

nodes.label: Applied Architecture Map
nodes.rationale: The module connects epistemology, materialization review, governance, table engineering, raw audits, derivable data, and live sources.

nodes.label: Scientific Vocabulary Freeze
nodes.rationale: TSIS must distinguish primitives, features, representations, states, decisions, outcomes, and knowledge before implementation.

nodes.label: Observation Abstraction Ladder
nodes.rationale: Observation, primitive, feature, representation, and state form successive scientific abstractions.

nodes.label: Event Research Layer
nodes.rationale: Event research extends market representation through governed questions, evidence, validation, knowledge, and memory.

nodes.label: Epistemological Architecture
nodes.rationale: Market representation and event research are coordinated parts of quantitative research epistemology.

nodes.label: Architecture Corpus Index
nodes.rationale: The index organizes representation, event, and discovery theory into one reading sequence.

nodes.label: Market Representation Architecture
nodes.rationale: TSIS prioritizes faithful, reproducible, temporally valid market representation before prediction or strategy.

nodes.label: Representation Before Prediction
nodes.rationale: Strategies consume market knowledge, while representation quality sets the ceiling for downstream intelligence.

nodes.label: Representation Precedes Intelligence
nodes.rationale: Features describe properties, states compose situations, and representations remain independent of models and strategies.

nodes.label: Market Knowledge Ontology
nodes.rationale: Reality becomes observation, observable, primitive, feature, representation, state, decision, and outcome through governed abstraction.

nodes.label: Representation Layer Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Observation, primitive, feature, representation, state, decision, and outcome layers have non-interchangeable responsibilities.

nodes.label: Canonical Primitives
nodes.rationale: Primitives are deterministic canonical market objects with identity, timestamps, ordering, and quality semantics.

nodes.label: Deterministic Observable Feature
nodes.rationale: A feature is a temporally legal deterministic function of canonical inputs that measures one observable property.

nodes.label: Coherent Domain Representation
nodes.rationale: A representation is a structured, versioned, internally consistent collection of related features describing one domain.

nodes.label: Temporally Legal State
nodes.rationale: A state is a point-in-time composition of legal representations and neither predicts nor recommends.

nodes.label: Prescriptive Decision Layer
nodes.rationale: A documented policy transforms valid observable states into actions without redefining market observations.

nodes.label: Post Decision Outcome Separation
nodes.rationale: Outcomes measure what occurs strictly after the reference timestamp and cannot participate in state construction.

nodes.label: Temporal Legality
nodes.rationale: Every state has one decision timestamp, excludes future information, and respects point-in-time availability.

nodes.label: Observable Eligibility
nodes.rationale: Only information with effective availability, canonical lineage, temporal legality, and sufficient quality may enter market representation.

nodes.label: Evidence Based Causality
nodes.rationale: Predictive association and feature importance do not establish causation; causal claims require rigorous experiments.

nodes.label: Canonical Feature Families
nodes.rationale: Every feature belongs to one primary semantic family with declared inputs, dimensions, timing, and quality boundaries.

nodes.label: Governed Feature Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: A feature advances through research idea, formal definition, prototype, validation, registration, materialization, and promotion without skipped stages.

nodes.label: Feature Materialization Modes
nodes.rationale: Registry existence and physical persistence are separate decisions governed by scope, population, cost, and consumer need.

nodes.label: Feature Registry Authority
nodes.rationale: A canonical feature officially exists only after registration in the single authoritative catalogue.

nodes.label: Representation Change Governance
nodes.rationale: Lower layers cannot redefine higher semantic authority, and every change is versioned, evidenced, and traceable.

nodes.label: Architectural Anti Patterns
nodes.rationale: TSIS forbids layer mixing, future leakage, strategy-shaped semantics, and direct canonical use of vendor fields.

nodes.label: Ontology Preserving Extensions
nodes.rationale: Future data, models, and representations extend the existing ontology rather than create parallel layers.

nodes.label: Representation Constitutional Principles
nodes.rationale: Market precedes strategy, observation precedes prediction, representation precedes intelligence, and semantics never drift silently.

nodes.label: Governed Feature Generation
nodes.rationale: A feature is a deterministic, observable, legally timed transformation of canonical primitives.

nodes.label: Canonical Feature Operators
nodes.rationale: Operators are the governed atomic mathematical transformations from which features are constructed.

nodes.label: Ordered Feature Transformations
nodes.rationale: Feature transformations preserve an explicit ordered pipeline in which normalization can change representation without changing meaning.

nodes.label: Multi Scale Feature Semantics
nodes.rationale: Each scale is explicit and represents a distinct canonical feature within a shared semantic family.

nodes.label: Point In Time Contextual Features Document
Point In Time Contextual Features
nodes.rationale: Context describes the environment around local observations and never contains future information.

nodes.label: Governed Composite Features
nodes.rationale: Composite features deterministically combine canonical features under one declared mathematical specification.

nodes.label: Interaction Feature Semantics
nodes.rationale: Interaction features measure joint behavior that no input feature expresses independently.

nodes.label: Canonical Meta Features
nodes.rationale: Meta-features deterministically measure behavior, stability, dynamics, or quality of canonical features.

nodes.label: Feature Validation Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Canonical promotion requires mathematical, semantic, temporal, data, reproducibility, and robustness validation.

nodes.label: Intrinsic Feature Quality
nodes.rationale: Feature quality is assessed before usefulness and independently of predictive performance.

nodes.label: Representation Before Feature Selection
nodes.rationale: Selection serves a consumer but never defines or shrinks the canonical feature universe.

nodes.label: Scope Relative Representation Completeness
nodes.rationale: Completeness is relative to declared observable dimensions, populations, horizons, sources, and known limitations.

nodes.label: Representation As Infrastructure
nodes.rationale: Market representation is strategy-independent scientific infrastructure from which knowledge and downstream systems emerge.

nodes.label: Scientific Event Definition
nodes.rationale: An event is a reproducible research anchor, not a trading opportunity, prediction, or strategy.

nodes.label: Canonical Event Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Every event belongs to one primary family so populations and research remain reproducible and unambiguous.

nodes.label: Event Family Semantics
nodes.rationale: Event families group research anchors with common observable meaning and boundaries rather than strategies.

nodes.label: Governed Event Population
nodes.rationale: The event population, not an isolated occurrence, is the scientific unit from which phenomena can be inferred.

nodes.label: Governed Event Windows
nodes.rationale: Event windows determine which observable states belong to an event investigation and make outcomes comparable.

nodes.label: Event Geometry
nodes.rationale: Event geometry measures how an event occupies time, state space, and market context independently of strategy.

nodes.label: Reproducible Event Candidate
nodes.rationale: A candidate is a timestamped detector output between representation and research, not yet an accepted event object.

nodes.label: Canonical Event State
nodes.rationale: Event State records what was observable within governed event context and is neither the event nor a strategy.

nodes.label: Post Event Outcomes
nodes.rationale: Event outcomes deterministically measure consequences after the anchor and remain separate from event-state observations.

nodes.label: Event Research Governance
nodes.rationale: Canonical event objects advance through explicit taxonomy, population, window, state, outcome, validation, and promotion rules.

nodes.label: Phenomenon Discovery Architecture
nodes.rationale: Scientific knowledge is discovered from reproducible states and validated phenomena before strategies emerge.

nodes.label: Evidence First Discovery
nodes.rationale: Representation organizes evidence, while phenomena emerge only from repeated comparable observations.

nodes.label: Governed Research Question
nodes.rationale: A research question freezes scope, population, observables, and required evidence before a phenomenon is proposed.

nodes.label: Falsifiable Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: A hypothesis is a provisional explanation with an explicit null and does not become knowledge before repeated validation.

nodes.label: Uncontaminated Evidence Collection
nodes.rationale: Evidence is observed reproducibly before interpretation and may support or reject a hypothesis.

nodes.label: Canonical Phenomenon Formation
nodes.rationale: A phenomenon is a strategy-independent empirical regularity promoted from reproducible population evidence.

nodes.label: Governed Knowledge Formation
nodes.rationale: A knowledge object organizes multiple validated phenomena into reusable conditional scientific understanding.

nodes.label: Knowledge Validation
nodes.rationale: Knowledge becomes canonical through reproducible scientific validation rather than profitability.

nodes.label: Strategy From Validated Knowledge
nodes.rationale: A strategy is a governed decision policy downstream of one or more validated knowledge objects.

nodes.label: Evidence Driven Knowledge Evolution
nodes.rationale: New evidence may strengthen, refine, restrict, falsify, or retire provisional knowledge.

nodes.label: Knowledge Registry Authority
nodes.rationale: Validated knowledge officially exists only when recorded with evidence, scope, limitations, lineage, and status in the canonical registry.

nodes.label: Governed Research Protocol
nodes.rationale: Institutional research uses explicit reproducible protocols and lineage so evidence rather than authority drives knowledge.

nodes.label: Research Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Research advances through frozen questions, protocols, evidence, analysis, validation, conclusions, and registry updates.

nodes.label: Institutional Research Memory
nodes.rationale: Research artifacts, including rejected hypotheses, persist as repository memory rather than conversational state.

nodes.label: Continuous Discovery Loop
nodes.rationale: Contradictions, new data, limitations, and stale knowledge create governed backlog items and renewed investigations.

nodes.label: Bounded Autonomous Discovery
nodes.rationale: Autonomous agents may propose and execute research steps but cannot promote canonical knowledge outside governance.

nodes.label: Canonical Materialization Bridge
nodes.rationale: A governed decision process separates semantic representation authority from engineering implementation.

nodes.label: Canonical Market Representation
nodes.rationale: A canonical representation is the authoritative conceptual account of market state or context and exists before physical artifacts.

nodes.label: Representation Justification
nodes.rationale: No representation enters implementation without explicit ontological, scientific, operational, and institutional justification.

nodes.label: Materialization Decision
nodes.rationale: Physical persistence is optional and requires a deliberate scope, consumer, cost, and governance decision.

nodes.label: Physical Representation
nodes.rationale: A physical representation is a governed institutional implementation that realizes but does not redefine canonical semantics.

nodes.label: Materialization Strategy
nodes.rationale: Architectural strategy determines how an approved physical representation exists before technology is selected.

nodes.label: Preimplementation Contracts
nodes.rationale: Representation, dataset, schema, quality, lineage, validation, and consumer contracts govern implementation before code runs.

nodes.label: Physical Realization
nodes.rationale: Engineering creates reproducible builders, schemas, manifests, validators, datasets, and operational evidence under approved contracts.

nodes.label: Institutional Certification
nodes.rationale: Certification establishes objective evidence that a physical implementation faithfully realizes its canonical representation.

nodes.label: Institutional Promotion
nodes.rationale: Promotion separately authorizes a certified representation for a declared institutional scope and consumer class.

nodes.label: Dual Representation Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Canonical semantic evolution and physical implementation evolution are independent but explicitly linked and versioned.

nodes.label: Bidirectional Architectural Traceability
nodes.rationale: Every physical artifact traces back to semantic authority, decisions, contracts, code, data, evidence, and promotion status.

nodes.label: Materialization Constitutional Principles
nodes.rationale: Semantic authority originates in canonical representation, architecture precedes engineering, and governance precedes materialization.
